MultiSolid graphical design: decisions and reconstruction guide

Design record and reproducible specification · 26 September 2026

This is the consolidated handoff for reproducing the graphical work or taking it in a different direction. It combines the brief, inspirations, accepted and rejected decisions, measured specifications, animation algorithm, source references, implementation map and verification history. The portable HTML edition embeds the screenshots and complete snapshots of the relevant presentation code and review tools. It can be read offline as one file; external references remain links.

The specification describes the implemented working tree, including changes that were not committed. The repository base is c145735c3e2b65bb21208c3e04256137b6f309cd; that commit alone does not contain this finished design. The HTML source appendix records file hashes so this design can be distinguished from later edits.

Brief, inspirations and provenance

The starting brief was deliberately expressive: the user asked to “Fontslop” the UI, go “Xenosystems” on it, and take an artistic direction. Those words were treated as permission for an unusual industrial/scientific identity: compressed typography, hard edges, warm paper against dark ink, an acid accent, and a strange sculptural process motif. These phrases were art direction rather than a named technical specification. No particular Xenosystems artwork, font package or stylesheet was supplied or copied.

The condensed display face, isolated italic serif line, lime/copper palette and fine wire envelope are design choices made for this app. “Technical publication”, “industrial instrument” and “editorial introduction” describe the intended effect; they are interpretations, not unrecorded external sources. The published references later in this guide provide scientific context and usability constraints, rather than a source for the exact colours or artwork.

The user's directions progressively made the brief more precise:

Direction from the conversationConsequence retained in the design
Be visually adventurous.Expressive welcome, distinctive masthead, cream/ink/lime identity.
Give the graphics and terminology scientific meaning.Replace the generic FLOW FIELD motif with cyclic packed-bed material states; use real quantities, units and process language.
The original packed-bed reforming concept uses three reactors.Keep a three-part visual motif. A software case still describes one bed; the artwork is not a plant configuration selector.
Heat can serve other applications, including combustion and power.Mention syngas, hydrogen, process heat and power; avoid implying that every cycle ends in reforming or produces syngas.
The first process figure looked too scientific.Abstract the process into packed forms, colour states and an orbit; remove flow arrows, reaction equations and equipment labels from the welcome.
The application looked acceptable but was difficult to author in.Give editing the full page, make plots optional, fix short menus and test an empty-project workflow.
Try a simple, slow animation.Add independent animation timing, a persistent pause setting and no timer work off-page.
Bring back the circles and helices.Stationary grains switch instantly, separately, around a stochastic moving front; the envelope rotates and changes colour smoothly.
Keep the earlier slight 3D effect.Use cylindrical projection, compressed and darker edges, brighter central particles, curved ends and front/back helix occlusion.
Half a turn was still too tightly wound; use one-sixth.Final winding is 1 / 6 turn, or 60 degrees, along the bed height.
Check 4:3 and 16:9.Evaluate 1024×768, 1280×960, 1280×720 and 1920×1080 logical window sizes.

What the supplied scientific images contributed

The six supplied images included two versions of a three-stage oxidation/reduction/ reforming arrangement; a two-bed state-switching sketch; an air/fuel reactor pair; a comparison of circulating solids with a gas-switched fixed bed; and a two-bed valve diagram with hot nitrogen and a carbon-dioxide/water stream. They supplied the logic of recurrent operation, solid-state changes and useful heat. The packed bed images supplied the granule motif. The two-reactor examples established wider chemical-looping context rather than replacing the requested three-part identity.

The images were not accompanied by complete bibliographic attribution. This guide does not assert which paper each image came from. Their role is recorded here as user-supplied visual references; the separately cited papers are independently identified scientific context. The external images are not bundled into the HTML. Its illustrations are captures of this app.

Copyable brief for a redesign

Build a distinctive, usable desktop for transient packed-bed simulation. Keep the expressive identity mainly on the welcome and masthead; use readable system type for scientific work. Combine warm paper, dark ink, acid lime and restrained copper with fine rules and square controls. Represent cycling states using three slightly three-dimensional packed forms: circles stay fixed and switch between two colours individually near moving fronts. Loose outer helices turn slowly and blend their colours; the final reference winding is one-sixth of a turn. Retain an obvious persistent pause control. Treat the motif as abstract identity, separate from calculated numerical previews. Make Chemistry, Bed and Program practical to author at small 4:3 and 16:9 sizes, with persistent Add actions and previews on demand. Preserve scientific quantities, units, precision, data and existing solver semantics. Judge the result by creating a case, as well as by its appearance.

MultiSolid should feel like a distinctive scientific instrument that people can comfortably use for repeated, detailed work. The direction keeps the warm paper, dark ink, lime accent and abstract packed-bed emblem from the visual exploration. It gives ordinary reading, numerical editing and evidence more prominence inside the workspace.

The first visual review missed a central failure: the interface could display an existing case while making a new one unnecessarily difficult to enter. Protecting the bed plot squeezed its settings into a scroll area. Program channels competed for space, and even short dropdowns scrolled. The user's rejection was correct. Readable screenshots and preserved scientific curves did not establish usable authoring.

This revision is tested by creating a reacting case from an empty project using Qt mouse and keyboard events. It keeps the paper/ink/lime identity, but gives editing the available space and opens graphs on demand. The captures below are from the native desktop, not mockups. The authoring case reaches Inputs ready; it is not represented as a completed simulation.

The design in use

The welcome carries expressive type and three packed beds of stationary circles. Each outer helix winds one-sixth of a turn along the bed, rotates once every 36 seconds, and gradually blends between lime and copper. Compressed, darker particles at the edges, brighter centres and curved ends give the beds a slight 3D effect. The circles switch colour instantly, individually, at randomly staggered times close to an upward-moving front. Each front takes 24 seconds; successive fronts alternate the two states. Random thresholds stay fixed during each sweep, so particles never flicker or change behaviour with frame rate. Pause is visible and remembered; the timer stops off-page.

Bed starts with geometry, material basis and thermal settings above the zone table. The numerical preview opens with Preview bed and returns to the same setup.

Program presents one channel at a time. The table has room for initial values, durations and targets; Add step stays visible when the rows scroll. The complete schedule is a separate preview. This costs one click to inspect a plot, but avoids making every editing task compete with a permanently displayed plot.

First-case workflow

  1. Create a project and a named case. A new case opens in Chemistry, where its species are defined before they become columns or feed fields elsewhere.
  2. Add gases and solids, then optional reaction families. Add buttons sit outside the lists. A draggable divider allocates space between species and reactions. The reaction network opens on demand.
  3. Enter Bed geometry and material zones. Adding another zone splits the last zone's extent; new material properties remain unfinished for explicit entry.
  4. In Program, set the initial feed and outlet pressure. Add holds and ramps. Feed targets identify retained flow/temperature, and the composition editor keeps its total and Normalize action outside the scrolling species fields. Channel tabs expose every channel without stacking several small tables.
  5. Set the total repeating simulation duration in General, along with numerical settings and requested outputs. Non-repeating duration still follows the steps. Incomplete drafts autosave; validation details explain what remains to be fixed.
  6. Return to the project. A ready case exposes its enabled Run action.

This remains an editor, not a wizard: users can move freely between pages and revisit any input. Chemistry selection, Bed and Program are the useful initial sequence; General contains numerical choices and the overall repeating horizon.

TrialWhat it established or missedDecision

The design review also exposed a subtle interaction issue: the old primary and dark button rules could override the general focus rule. Focus now has explicit role-aware styling, verified on rendered widgets after Tab navigation.

Semantic status colours are separate from the brand accent: green for ready or succeeded, blue for activity, amber for attention/staleness, red for failed operations, grey for neutral states. Every status retains readable words. “Inputs ready” means structural checks passed, not that the physical assumptions or numerical results have been scientifically validated.

Primary actions use lime, routine actions a light surface, and the smaller case-creation action may use dark ink. Destructive controls retain explicit action names or accessible labels. Checkboxes use a visible frame plus a check or mixed mark; selection is not communicated through hue alone. Controls keep their size when gaining focus by compensating border thickness with padding.

Composition, density and behaviour

The welcome pairs an editorial introduction with abstract cycling-state artwork. It does not prescribe a plant layout, represent computed fronts or imply that every application makes syngas. The copy also recognises hydrogen, process heat and power. A case represents one packed bed and its operating program.

Project pages prioritise the case table and run state. Counts are actual integers, not decorative zero-padded counters. Functional pages have ordinary names. Tables keep stable columns, visible headers and textual states. Long case names and run-state labels have complete tooltips.

Editing uses the full page at every tested size. Bed settings remain above its zone table, and Program options stay above the selected channel. Add buttons remain outside table scrolling. Long lists still scroll; the difference is that scrolling belongs to the content, not to a stack of competing editor and preview panels. Chemistry's divider lets users allocate space to the list they are working with. The compact case toolbar returns vertical space to the editor.

The two- and three-item dropdowns show all their options. Larger menus may still scroll normally. Control and popup sizes use Qt logical pixels, including under 200% device scaling.

For the short-menu fix, the measured defect was in this application's styling: viewport padding clipped the final row. Keep popup viewport padding at zero and put horizontal padding on the items instead. The retained QSS is:

QComboBox { padding-right: 25px; combobox-popup: 0; }
QComboBox QAbstractItemView {
    selection-background-color: #d9f36d;
    padding: 0;
    border: 1px solid #858978;
}
QComboBox QAbstractItemView::item { min-height: 26px; padding: 0 8px; }

Check the opened popup itself: two and three items must all fit in the viewport with a vertical scrollbar maximum of zero. A larger menu may scroll. Do not assume that changing maxVisibleItems alone fixes a stylesheet geometry problem. The Qt API and style-sheet references are listed below; the clipping diagnosis came from native measurements in this app.

Scientific content

Show units with quantities and distinguish physical settings from numerical settings. “Output sampling interval” is not an integrator time step; “axial cells” is discretisation; concentration basis and gas storage volume retain their physical distinctions. Scientific tooltips explain these choices without changing their input keys or solver meaning.

Embedded input previews use six dark colours and five stroke patterns, producing 30 combinations before repetition. The nine-species example is explicitly checked. Colours identify series within a plot, not universal species identities across projects. Curves retain their actual samples, coordinates and units. Exported scientific plots keep their existing presentation.

The six preview colours are #0072b2, #be492b, #007a5e, #924c8e, #875800, #56616d. The five strokes are solid, dashed, dash-dot, dotted and the Matplotlib custom sequence (0, (5, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1)). Index the colour by i % 6 and the stroke by i % 5, with width 1.6. Single flow, temperature and pressure curves use the darker copper and width 1.5. The gas legend sits above the composition axes at (0, 1.02), lower-left anchored, three columns, 8 pt. Plot backgrounds use paper/surface, ticks 8 pt muted, labels ink, and only the left and bottom spines remain. Matplotlib font sizes here are points, not Qt pixels. These are presentation settings for input previews, not transformations of data.

The reaction network keeps its gas/solid/reaction categories, explanatory key, missing-species indication and Graphviz layout. The redesign changes its placement and integration into the paper-coloured workspace, not its scientific topology.

The scientific interpretation continues to draw on the user's supplied diagrams, Spallina et al. on packed-bed reforming and packed-bed CLC heat management. The illustration remains an identity asset, clearly separate from those calculated previews.

Reconstructing the final animation

The animation is native QPainter code, not an image-generation prompt, a video background or a pre-rendered sprite. Its geometry is an artistic construction; no solver values drive it. The full welcome_animation.py snapshot in the HTML appendix is the reference when exact reproduction is needed.

Parameters and independent clocks

ParameterFinal value
Beds3; centres at x = −155, 0, +155 in artwork coordinates
Grains26 rows × 11 columns = 286 per bed; 858 total
Two-state period48 s; one upward sweep every 24 s
Bed timing offsets0, 16, 32 s
Helix rotationOne revolution in 36 s; extra phase 0.7 radians per bed
Helix winding along bed1/6 turn = 60°; separate from rotation speed
Helices8 strands, 97 samples along each strand
Helix colour cycle60 s; bed offset 2π/3 and strand offset 0.45 radians
Repaint request interval33 ms, approximately 30 Hz; elapsed time drives the state
Grain coloursLime #d9f36d and copper #d79a72; instant binary switching
Overall tilt−12°
OrbitEllipse x = −252, y = −72, width 504, height 144; 1 px line in #61694c
Fit scalemin((width - 44) / 520, (height - 112) / 270)
TranslationWidget centre, with artwork centre 4 px above vertical centre
Pause preferenceQSettings key appearance/pause_welcome_animation

The 48 seconds describe the two-state timing, not an exactly repeating movie: each sweep receives a new random pattern, while rotation and colour blending have their own periods. The 24-second GIF produced during review is only an excerpt.

Stationary particles and slight 3D depth

Use a seeded Python Random(731) for the fixed positions. For row r = 0…25 and column c = 0…10, in row-major order:

theta = -pi / 2 + (c + 0.25 * (r % 2)) * pi / 10
x = 33 * sin(theta) + uniform(-0.12, 0.12)
y = (r - 12.5) * 7.2 + 4 * cos(theta) + uniform(-0.2, 0.2)
depth = sqrt(max(0, 1 - (x / 33) ** 2))
circle_radius = 1.45 + 1.4 * depth
circle_alpha = round(100 + 155 * depth)

The projection compresses the particles toward the cylindrical edges, while the centre has larger and brighter circles. Rows curve slightly at the ends. The tiny position jitter prevents a perfectly machined lattice; it is generated once, not per frame. All three beds share this position template. Particle size and opacity stay fixed during playback, so changing chemical colour remains instantaneous.

Behind the circles, draw a 70-wide body between y = −102 and +102, using curved ends with control points reaching ±111. A horizontal linear gradient runs through #191e17 at 0, #343a2c at 0.38, #292f23 at 0.7 and #191e17 at 1. Draw the top ellipse in the rectangle (−35, −109, 70, 14) with a subtle #626c50 0.6-width edge. These cues make a shallow cylinder; no actual 3D engine is needed.

Stochastic moving front without flicker

For bed b and elapsed seconds t, compute:

sweep_time = (t + b * 48 / 3) / 24
sweep = floor(sweep_time)
progress = sweep_time - sweep

For that bed and sweep, seed a separate generator with 1709 + b * 101 + sweep * 7919. Each fixed particle receives a threshold:

raw = (96 - y) / 192 + 0.018 * sin(x / 12) + uniform(-0.065, 0.065)
point = 0.025 + 0.95 * (raw - min(all_raw)) / (max(all_raw) - min(all_raw))
lime_state = (progress >= point) != bool(sweep % 2)

Large positive y is the bottom, so it changes first. Random offsets spread the events around a narrow front instead of switching complete rows. The state is a boolean: a grain jumps directly between the two colours and stays there until the next front. Odd sweeps reverse the colour change while still moving upward. Thresholds are cached, with a maximum of 12 bed/sweep schedules. Never draw a new random state on each frame: that would create flicker instead of a front.

Individual events have their own thresholds, but several may fall within one display frame. The design requirement is separate, discrete grain transitions, not an artificial restriction to exactly one changed pixel or grain per frame. Use the captured Python code for the exact seeded sequence when porting to another language; a different PRNG can preserve the visual logic without reproducing every grain's timing exactly.

Loose rotating helices and drawing order

For strand s = 0…7 and axial fraction u = 0…1, sampled in 96 intervals:

rotation = t * 2 * pi / 36 + b * 0.7
angle = s * 2 * pi / 8 + rotation + u * 2 * pi * (1 / 6)
depth = sin(angle)
radius = 44 + 4 * sin(pi * u)
x = radius * cos(angle)
y = -108 + 216 * u + 7 * depth
front_facing = depth >= 0
blend = (1 + sin(t * 2 * pi / 60 + b * 2 * pi / 3 + s * 0.45)) / 2

Linearly blend the copper and lime RGB channels using blend. Split each strand's path into back and front portions. Paint in this order: ink background, orbit, back helices, shaded body and top, fixed circles, front helices, end rings, then captions and the pause control. Back helix alpha/width are 75/0.8; front values are 175/0.85. Draw outer end rings in (−44, end−7, 88, 14) for end = ±108, with #8c9677 at width 0.65. Back/front occlusion is essential to the depth effect.

The final loose winding followed trials at 0.85 turn and half a turn. Do not accidentally restore 0.5 while copying an earlier preview. Changing HELIX_TURNS changes the shape along the bed; changing HELIX_ROTATION_SECONDS changes how quickly that shape spins. They are independent.

Motion lifecycle and useful adjustments

Use QElapsedTimer plus stored elapsed seconds. Stop and invalidate the elapsed clock when paused or hidden; restart it from the stored position when shown and playing. The 33 ms timer requests repaint, rather than incrementing an angle by a fixed amount. This prevents a slower computer from changing the animation speed. Pause/Play is keyboard-operable and the preference survives opening a new window. There is no claim that the current code detects an OS reduced-motion preference; the implemented control is the persistent explicit pause option.

If you want to change…Adjust…Preserve…
Helix loosenessHELIX_TURNS; current 1/6, zero gives untwisted strands.Rotation clock and front timing.
Rotation speedHELIX_ROTATION_SECONDS; larger means slower.Axial winding.
Front speedPERIOD_SECONDS; one sweep is half the value.Binary transitions and bed offsets derived from the period.
Front roughnessRandom threshold jitter, currently ±0.065; curvature term 0.018.Fixed thresholds throughout each sweep.
Granule densityRow/column counts and spacing, then recalibrate projection/radius.Stationary positions and enough visible separation to read circles.
Perceived depthEdge compression, spatial opacity/radius and shell gradient.Back/front occlusion; avoid replacing the circles with flat bars.
Colour driftThe 60 s helix colour period and palette endpoints.No smooth colour interpolation on the grains themselves.
Application meaningCopy and captions.Broad heat/reforming/combustion scope and the distinction between artwork and calculated data.

Implementation map and reconstruction sequence

The app is Python/PyQt6 with Matplotlib previews. The reviewed local environment reports Python 3.11.9, PyQt6 6.10.2, Qt 6.10.0 and Matplotlib 3.10.8. These identify the capture environment, not a new dependency lock. desktop/pyproject.toml declares Python ≥3.11 and <3.13. The animation has no new runtime dependency.

tools/design_review.pyNative presentation, contrast, focus, dropdown and numerical-preview checks.
tools/authoring_review.pyEmpty-project case creation by actual Qt mouse/keyboard events.
tests/test_identity.py, test_editor.py, test_window.pyAnimation lifecycle and authoring/navigation regressions.

The HTML appendix contains full-file snapshots for this map, along with recorded audit evidence. They include existing application logic as context; not every line was introduced by the graphical redesign. The snapshots are a presentation-layer handoff, not the entire solver repository or a standalone runnable application. The package declares GPL-3.0-only; preserve the project's licence context when reusing its code.

Reproduce this version

  1. Start from the working MultiSolid repository and its documented environment. Keep domain models, input schemas and the execution engine available. Compare the included full-file snapshots with the target checkout before applying them.
  2. Install the palette, fonts and QSS before creating widgets. Include assets/*.svg as package data so checkboxes, chevrons and the application icon work after packaging as well as from the source tree.
  3. Recreate the masthead and welcome composition. Apply the 64 px wordmark override and 5:6 hero ratio. Pass the existing application settings to the animation.
  4. Implement the packed circles and front scheduler as fixed geometry plus an elapsed-time function. Add helices and front/back layering. Confirm 1/6 turn, instant grain transitions, smooth helix colours and persistent pause.
  5. Recreate AuthoringWorkspace: edit and preview pages share the available area. Preserve the underlying controls while toggling, draw a hidden plot when it is shown, and allow inspection navigation in read-only mode.
  6. Rebuild Bed and Program layouts around their editing tables. Keep Add actions visible; preserve mode data, outlet pressure, units and precision. Add Chemistry's resizable species/reaction split and start new cases there.
  7. Apply semantic status/focus treatments and revised terminology consistently. Keep calculated figures tied to real preview arrays. Style embedded previews separately from exported scientific plots.
  8. Run the checks below and inspect small-window captures before increasing the density or adding ornament. Recheck popup geometry on the target Qt/platform.

To redo the visual direction instead, preserve these functional behaviours first. Change identity and theme tokens next, then artwork. Evaluate each revision by authoring the same case; a successful imported-case screenshot alone is inadequate. Use the source appendix as a reference, not a reason to overwrite unrelated newer application work.

Annotated reference list

The user brief, the supplied diagrams and the observed UI failures are primary inputs to the design. The following published references support particular decisions; none specifies the exact MultiSolid palette, fonts or helix geometry. References were checked while consolidating this guide. Third-party pages may change; the embedded implementation snapshots preserve the actual result.

ReferenceSpecific use and attribution boundary
IBM Carbon — Typography style strategiesSupports separating expressive introductory moments from sustained productive work. The chosen Impact/Georgia/system-font combination is ours, not Carbon's prescribed type set.
IBM Carbon — SpacingSupports using consistent spacing increments to express grouping and hierarchy. The app uses a related 8/12/16/24 rhythm with local corrections.
Kelley Gordon, NN/g — Visual Hierarchy in UX: DefinitionSupports deliberate scale, contrast and grouping so decoration does not compete with user content.
Jakob Nielsen, NN/g — 10 Usability HeuristicsSupports visible status, familiar language, consistency and recovery. Full-page editing was a response to this app's observed failures, not a layout copied from the article.
W3C — Contrast (Minimum), SC 1.4.3Source for the 4.5:1 ordinary-text contrast criterion used by the audit.
W3C — Non-text Contrast, SC 1.4.11Source for the 3:1 criterion applied to essential control boundaries and visual identification.
W3C — Focus Visible, SC 2.4.7Supports a visible keyboard location. The two-pixel blue treatment and selector fixes are implementation decisions.
W3C — Use of Color, SC 1.4.1Supports state words and other cues in addition to colour.
Masataka Okabe and Kei Ito — Color Universal DesignSupports redundant identification of plotted series. The six colours and five strokes here form our own combination, not a claim to reproduce or certify a CUD palette.
Spallina et al., 2017 — Chemical looping reforming in packed-bed reactors: Modelling, experimental validation and large-scale reactor designScientific context for dynamically operated packed beds and sequential oxidation, reduction and reforming. Fuel Processing Technology 156, pp. 156–170; DOI 10.1016/j.fuproc.2016.10.014. It grounds process meaning, not a mandatory three-vessel software model or the invented helices.
Spallina et al., 2013 — Investigation of heat management for CLC of syngas in packed bed reactorsScientific context for heat management in cyclic packed-bed combustion and integration with power systems. Supports broadening the copy beyond reforming products. It does not validate the artwork's timing or geometry.
Qt — QComboBox and Qt Style Sheets ReferenceImplementation references for popup views, sizing and native widget styling. The two-item clipping bug and its fix were measured locally.
Qt — QPainter, QElapsedTimer, QTimerReconstruction references for vector painting, elapsed-time state and repaint scheduling. The current documentation may describe a newer Qt release than the recorded 6.10 capture environment.
Python 3.11 — randomReconstruction reference for seeded local random generators. The particular seeds, threshold formula and front roughness are original implementation choices.

No generative image service, purchased bitmap asset or external font download is required to reproduce the current artwork. Native shapes, native text, local SVG controls and code-generated colours produce the result.

Feedback and recovery

Saving, ready, invalid-input and save-failure states use distinct text and visual treatments. An invalid draft exposes Details…, which opens the full validation text in a selectable, read-only dialog. It can be opened with the keyboard and closed with Escape. Detailed paths belong there rather than overwhelming the status strip. A persistence failure keeps the editor dirty and visibly reports the error; a successful retry restores ready status.

Validation and reproduction

Two tools check different things. tools/authoring_review.py creates a project and case through QTest clicks and keystrokes, including real modal dialogs, table cells and dropdowns. It never imports a case or fills input documents through model setters. Reading the saved project is used only for verification.

The authoring audit records successful creation at:

Aspect ratioWindow dimensionsResult
4:31024 × 768Case created, saved and ready to run
4:31280 × 960Case created, saved and ready to run
16:91280 × 720Case created, saved and ready to run
16:91920 × 1080Case created, saved and ready to run

Each run selects six gases, two solids, three reactions, two material zones, three feed steps and three requested reports. It checks exact saved zone geometry and properties, initial feed values, a partial composition ramp, pressure, repeat state and a 42-second horizon. It switches away from Feed mode and back before checking persistence. The two zones and three steps are entered without scrolling their editing tables. The review rejects unavailable/clipped control hit points and any window growth beyond the requested dimensions.

The 200% authoring audit repeats this workflow at 1024 × 768 logical pixels. That tests scaled controls; it does not claim a 2048 × 1536 physical capture is a 1024 × 768 physical monitor.

Animation checks compare actual frames before and after waiting, verify an unchanged paused frame, resume playback, and verify that the timer stops off-page. A separate functional test checks pause persistence across newly constructed widgets and excludes hidden time from animation progression.

tools/design_review.py remains a complementary presentation check using a supplied example. It checks contrast, keyboard focus, invalid input feedback, save failure recovery, preview geometry and exact agreement with the engine preview arrays. It opens Bed/Program previews explicitly and checks that composition legends sit outside the plotted data. It also measures two- and three-item popup viewports. Its native audit and 200% audit are separate from the case-creation evidence.

.venv\Scripts\python.exe desktop/tools/authoring_review.py
.venv\Scripts\python.exe desktop/tools/design_review.py
$env:QT_SCALE_FACTOR = '2'
.venv\Scripts\python.exe desktop/tools/authoring_review.py --size 1024x768 --output build/usability/scale-2
.venv\Scripts\python.exe desktop/tools/design_review.py --output build/design-review/scale-2
Remove-Item Env:QT_SCALE_FACTOR

Active body text against paper measures 13.25:1, supporting text 4.98:1, input boundaries 3.14:1, and focus against lime 5.86:1. Status text retains explicit words. These checks are useful criteria for a native application, not complete accessibility certification. Primary-action focus and checkbox focus specimens show actual Tab-navigation states.

The recorded authoring-layout regression run passed 108 tests with one skip for a POSIX-only Graphviz helper. Two DAETools deprecation warnings were emitted. An earlier concurrent run hit a 10-second worker-start deadline; that test passed in isolation and in the final 108-test run without changing worker code or timeouts. The later packed-circle animation revision passed three focused tests for pause, front progression and welcome navigation. The final one-sixth-turn render check confirmed advance, pause, resume and fit at all four requested window sizes. These are results recorded during implementation, not claims of a new full-suite run each time this document is rebuilt.

.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest desktop/tests/test_editor.py desktop/tests/test_window.py desktop/tests/test_identity.py desktop/tests/test_preview.py desktop/tests/test_graph_view.py desktop/tests/test_report.py desktop/tests/test_study_editor.py desktop/tests/test_project_results.py -q
.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest desktop/tests/test_identity.py desktop/tests/test_window.py::test_window_opens_on_welcome_then_project_case_list -q

Both presentation audit runs recorded 58 captures, nine focusable control specimens and six interaction/data checks. Native captures at both aspect ratios and the scaled small-window captures were visually inspected. The tests validate authored inputs and interaction mechanics; no new reacting solver run was performed by the authoring review. Full historical detail is retained in the verification record, also embedded in the HTML.

The prior broad test run found two existing Windows recent-path casing failures. They remain outside this layout change. The current review is Windows-specific; very large mechanisms, other platforms, assistive technology and scientists' real working sessions remain useful further evaluation. Creating a case by automation finds mechanical failures but does not measure a first-time user's comprehension or task speed. A future study should observe hesitation and mistakes when defining a cycle, repairing an invalid feed and comparing outputs.

Maintaining the design

Keep palette, type, focus and semantic colours in packed_bed_ui/theme.py, the masthead in identity.py, and the animation in welcome_animation.py. Use native widgets and existing role selectors. Preserve scientific schemas, calculations and export formatting independently of presentation. For authoring-layout changes, repeat the empty-project workflow at the small 4:3 and 16:9 sizes before judging screenshots. For preview changes, check plotted arrays as well as axes and labels.

Update this Markdown guide when making a design decision, then regenerate its portable edition with:

.venv\Scripts\python.exe desktop/tools/build_design_guide.py

The generated desktop/MultiSolid-design-guide.html includes source snapshots, file hashes, audit records and all referenced screenshots as embedded data. No network connection is needed to read it. For an exact comparison, retain that HTML file before regenerating it against later code. The primary references remain external links for attribution and further reading.

"""The desktop's ink, paper and acid visual language.

Keep presentation here: the theme does not change saved inputs or plot exports.
Fonts use local fallbacks so installed and frozen applications work offline.
"""

from functools import lru_cache
from pathlib import Path

from PyQt6.QtGui import QColor, QFont, QFontDatabase, QPalette
from PyQt6.QtWidgets import QApplication, QLabel


PAPER = "#f1f0e8"
SURFACE = "#faf9f3"
INK = "#242720"
MUTED = "#65685c"
LINE = "#d0d1c4"
BOUNDARY = "#858978"
FOCUS = "#245b83"
ACID = "#d9f36d"
ORANGE = "#be492b"
# Semantic tones are deliberately separate from the lime identity accent.
STATE_COLORS = {
    "neutral": ("#e7e9df", MUTED),
    "success": ("#e0ecc0", "#3d5028"),
    "warning": ("#ede3c9", "#715926"),
    "error": ("#f2ddd4", "#9b3d2a"),
    "active": ("#ddeaf3", "#245b83"),
}
# Dark categorical strokes on the light preview surface; dashes supplement hue.
PREVIEW_COLORS = ("#0072b2", "#be492b", "#007a5e", "#924c8e", "#875800", "#56616d")
PREVIEW_STYLES = ("-", "--", "-.", ":", (0, (5, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1)))
ASSETS = Path(__file__).with_name("assets")


@lru_cache(maxsize=16)
def font_family(*candidates):
    available = set(QFontDatabase.families())
    return next((name for name in candidates if name in available), QApplication.font().family())


def label(text, role, *, wrap=False):
    widget = QLabel(text)
    widget.setProperty("role", role)
    widget.setWordWrap(wrap)
    return widget


def series_style(index):
    """A redundant colour/stroke encoding for a series within an input preview."""
    return {"color": PREVIEW_COLORS[index % len(PREVIEW_COLORS)],
            "linestyle": PREVIEW_STYLES[index % len(PREVIEW_STYLES)], "linewidth": 1.6}


def apply_theme(app):
    """Install once, before creating widgets (including their native icons)."""
    if app.property("multisolid_theme"):
        return
    app.setProperty("multisolid_theme", True)
    app.setStyle("Fusion")
    body = font_family("Segoe UI", "Helvetica Neue", "DejaVu Sans")
    mono = font_family("Cascadia Mono", "Consolas", "DejaVu Sans Mono")
    display = font_family("Impact", "Arial Narrow", "DejaVu Sans")
    serif = font_family("Georgia", "Liberation Serif", "DejaVu Serif")
    font = QFont(body)
    font.setPointSizeF(10)
    app.setFont(font)
    palette = QPalette()
    for role, color in {
        QPalette.ColorRole.Window: PAPER,
        QPalette.ColorRole.WindowText: INK,
        QPalette.ColorRole.Base: SURFACE,
        QPalette.ColorRole.AlternateBase: "#ebece3",
        QPalette.ColorRole.Text: INK,
        QPalette.ColorRole.Button: PAPER,
        QPalette.ColorRole.ButtonText: INK,
        QPalette.ColorRole.BrightText: SURFACE,
        QPalette.ColorRole.Highlight: ACID,
        QPalette.ColorRole.HighlightedText: INK,
        QPalette.ColorRole.ToolTipBase: INK,
        QPalette.ColorRole.ToolTipText: SURFACE,
        QPalette.ColorRole.Link: ORANGE,
        QPalette.ColorRole.Mid: LINE,
        QPalette.ColorRole.Light: SURFACE,
        QPalette.ColorRole.Dark: MUTED,
        QPalette.ColorRole.PlaceholderText: MUTED,
    }.items():
        palette.setColor(role, QColor(color))
    for role in (QPalette.ColorRole.Text, QPalette.ColorRole.ButtonText, QPalette.ColorRole.WindowText):
        palette.setColor(QPalette.ColorGroup.Disabled, role, QColor("#888b7e"))
    app.setPalette(palette)
    app.setStyleSheet(STYLES.replace("@body", body).replace("@mono", mono)
                      .replace("@display", display).replace("@serif", serif)
                      .replace("@boundary", BOUNDARY).replace("@focus", FOCUS)
                      .replace("@assets", ASSETS.as_posix()))


def style_figure(figure):
    """Style only embedded previews, leaving the engine's exported plots alone."""
    figure.set_facecolor(PAPER)
    for axis in figure.axes:
        axis.set_facecolor(SURFACE)
        axis.tick_params(colors=MUTED, labelsize=8)
        axis.xaxis.label.set_color(INK)
        axis.yaxis.label.set_color(INK)
        axis.title.set_color(INK)
        axis.title.set_fontsize(10)
        axis.title.set_fontweight("medium")
        for position, spine in axis.spines.items():
            spine.set_color(LINE)
            spine.set_visible(position in ("left", "bottom"))
        axis.grid(color=LINE, alpha=0.6, linewidth=0.6)
        legend = axis.get_legend()
        if legend:
            legend.get_frame().set_facecolor(SURFACE)
            legend.get_frame().set_edgecolor(LINE)
            for text in legend.get_texts():
                text.set_color(INK)

def welcome_hero(create, open_project, settings=None):

    from PyQt6.QtWidgets import QFrame, QPushButton



    frame = QFrame()

    frame.setObjectName("welcomeHero")

    frame.setMinimumHeight(380)

    frame.setMaximumHeight(420)

    layout = QHBoxLayout(frame)

    layout.setContentsMargins(0, 0, 0, 0)

    layout.setSpacing(0)

    introduction = QWidget()

    content = QVBoxLayout(introduction)

    content.setContentsMargins(24, 24, 24, 24)

    content.setSpacing(8)

    content.addWidget(label("DYNAMIC PACKED-BED SIMULATION", "eyebrow"))

    title = label("MULTISOLID", "display")

    title.setStyleSheet('font-size: 64px;')

    content.addWidget(title)

    content.addWidget(label("Cyclic gas–solid processes.", "processTitle", wrap=True))

    content.addWidget(label("Resolve reactions, heat storage and axial profiles in packed beds "

                            "with changing gas feeds.", "muted", wrap=True))

    content.addWidget(label("Syngas & hydrogen. Process heat & power.", "muted", wrap=True))

    content.addWidget(label("Each case models one packed bed and its operating program.", "muted", wrap=True))

    content.addStretch()

    actions = QHBoxLayout()

    actions.setSpacing(8)

    for text, callback, role in (

        ("Create new project…", create, "primary"),

        ("Open existing project…", open_project, "secondary"),

    ):

        button = QPushButton(text)

        button.setProperty("role", role)

        button.setCursor(Qt.CursorShape.PointingHandCursor)

        button.setMinimumHeight(28)

        button.clicked.connect(callback)

        actions.addWidget(button)

    actions.addStretch()

    content.addLayout(actions)

    layout.addWidget(introduction, 5)

    layout.addWidget(CycleEmblem(settings=settings), 6)

    return frame

SHA-256 6015c605d711971721b5499c5c3f95a521bd84b41f13de86e19a138317c5ab58

"""A slow, pausable identity animation; never a calculated process preview."""

from functools import lru_cache
from math import cos, floor, pi, sin
from random import Random

from PyQt6.QtCore import QElapsedTimer, QPointF, QRectF, Qt, QTimer
from PyQt6.QtGui import QColor, QFont, QLinearGradient, QPainter, QPainterPath, QPen
from PyQt6.QtWidgets import QPushButton, QSizePolicy, QWidget

from .theme import ACID, INK, font_family


PARTICLE_COLUMNS = 11


def _packed_circles():
    random = Random(731)
    circles = []
    for row in range(26):
        for column in range(PARTICLE_COLUMNS):
            theta = -pi / 2 + (column + .25 * (row % 2)) * pi / (PARTICLE_COLUMNS - 1)
            # Project a cylindrical surface: compressed edges and gently curved rows.
            circles.append((33 * sin(theta) + random.uniform(-.12, .12),
                            (row - 12.5) * 7.2 + 4 * cos(theta) + random.uniform(-.2, .2)))
    return tuple(circles)


PARTICLES = _packed_circles()


@lru_cache(maxsize=12)
def _switch_points(bed, sweep):
    """One fixed, random switching time per grain for this upward sweep.

    Spatially bounded jitter scatters the transition around a moving front.
    Sampling at paint time would cause flicker; this schedule is independent of
    frame rate, and changes only when the next front enters the bed.
    """
    random = Random(1709 + bed * 101 + sweep * 7919)
    positions = [(96 - y) / 192 + .018 * sin(x / 12) + random.uniform(-.065, .065)
                 for x, y in PARTICLES]
    low, high = min(positions), max(positions)
    return tuple(.025 + .95 * (position - low) / (high - low) for position in positions)


class CycleEmblem(QWidget):
    """Packed circles switch state behind slowly rotating, colour-shifting helices.

    Three phase offsets evoke cyclic operation without prescribing reactor
    connections, products or calculated conversion fronts. Time advances only
    while visible and playing; the user's pause preference survives relaunches.
    """

    PERIOD_SECONDS = 48
    HELIX_ROTATION_SECONDS = 36
    HELIX_TURNS = 1 / 6
    COPPER = "#d79a72"
    PAUSE_KEY = "appearance/pause_welcome_animation"

    def __init__(self, parent=None, *, settings=None):
        super().__init__(parent)
        self.settings = settings
        self.paused = settings.value(self.PAUSE_KEY, False, type=bool) if settings is not None else False
        self._seconds = 0.0
        self._clock = QElapsedTimer()
        self.timer = QTimer(self)
        self.timer.setInterval(33)
        self.timer.timeout.connect(self.update)
        self.setMinimumWidth(350)
        self.setSizePolicy(QSizePolicy.Policy.Expanding, QSizePolicy.Policy.Expanding)
        self.setAccessibleName("Cycling states animation")
        self.setAccessibleDescription(
            "Three beds of stationary circles switch between lime and copper, grain by grain, "
            "around upward-moving fronts. Outer helices rotate and gradually change colour. "
            "An abstract motif of material states and retained heat."
        )
        self.pause_button = QPushButton(self)
        self.pause_button.setProperty("role", "artControl")
        self.pause_button.clicked.connect(lambda: self.set_paused(not self.paused))
        self._update_button()

    @property
    def seconds(self):
        return self._seconds + (self._clock.elapsed() / 1000 if self._clock.isValid() else 0)

    def _start(self):
        if not self.paused and self.isVisible() and not self.timer.isActive():
            self._clock.start()
            self.timer.start()

    def _stop(self):
        self._seconds = self.seconds
        self._clock.invalidate()
        self.timer.stop()

    def _update_button(self):
        self.pause_button.setText("Play animation" if self.paused else "Pause animation")
        self.pause_button.setAccessibleName(self.pause_button.text())
        self.pause_button.adjustSize()
        self.pause_button.move(self.width() - self.pause_button.width() - 16,
                               self.height() - self.pause_button.height() - 12)

    def set_paused(self, paused):
        self._stop()
        self.paused = bool(paused)
        if self.settings is not None:
            self.settings.setValue(self.PAUSE_KEY, self.paused)
        self._update_button()
        self._start()
        self.update()

    def showEvent(self, event):
        super().showEvent(event)
        self._start()

    def hideEvent(self, event):
        self._stop()
        super().hideEvent(event)

    def resizeEvent(self, event):
        super().resizeEvent(event)
        self._update_button()

    @classmethod
    def particle_states(cls, bed, seconds):
        sweep_time = (seconds + bed * cls.PERIOD_SECONDS / 3) / (cls.PERIOD_SECONDS / 2)
        sweep = floor(sweep_time)
        progress = sweep_time - sweep
        return tuple((progress >= point) != bool(sweep % 2) for point in _switch_points(bed, sweep))

    @staticmethod
    def _blend(first, second, amount):
        return QColor.fromRgbF(
            first.redF() * (1 - amount) + second.redF() * amount,
            first.greenF() * (1 - amount) + second.greenF() * amount,
            first.blueF() * (1 - amount) + second.blueF() * amount,
        )

    def _helices(self, bed, seconds):
        rotation = seconds * 2 * pi / self.HELIX_ROTATION_SECONDS + bed * .7
        colour_phase = seconds * 2 * pi / 60 + bed * 2 * pi / 3
        lime, copper = QColor(ACID), QColor(self.COPPER)
        helices = []
        for strand in range(8):
            back, front = QPainterPath(), QPainterPath()
            previous, previous_front = None, None
            for step in range(97):
                t = step / 96
                angle = strand * 2 * pi / 8 + rotation + t * 2 * pi * self.HELIX_TURNS
                depth = sin(angle)
                radius = 44 + 4 * sin(pi * t)
                point = QPointF(radius * cos(angle), -108 + 216 * t + 7 * depth)
                in_front = depth >= 0
                path = front if in_front else back
                if previous is None:
                    path.moveTo(point)
                else:
                    if in_front != previous_front:
                        path.moveTo(previous)
                    path.lineTo(point)
                previous, previous_front = point, in_front
            colour = self._blend(copper, lime, (1 + sin(colour_phase + strand * .45)) / 2)
            helices.append((back, front, colour))
        return helices

    def _bed(self, painter, bed, seconds):
        painter.save()
        painter.translate((bed - 1) * 155, 0)
        helices = self._helices(bed, seconds)
        painter.setBrush(Qt.BrushStyle.NoBrush)
        for back, _, colour in helices:
            colour.setAlpha(75)
            painter.setPen(QPen(colour, .8))
            painter.drawPath(back)

        # The grains stay fixed. Only their binary state changes; no crossfade.
        shell = QPainterPath()
        shell.moveTo(-35, -102)
        shell.cubicTo(-35, -111, 35, -111, 35, -102)
        shell.lineTo(35, 102)
        shell.cubicTo(35, 111, -35, 111, -35, 102)
        shell.closeSubpath()
        shade = QLinearGradient(-35, 0, 35, 0)
        shade.setColorAt(0, QColor("#191e17"))
        shade.setColorAt(.38, QColor("#343a2c"))
        shade.setColorAt(.7, QColor("#292f23"))
        shade.setColorAt(1, QColor("#191e17"))
        painter.fillPath(shell, shade)
        painter.setBrush(shade)
        painter.setPen(QPen(QColor("#626c50"), .6))
        painter.drawEllipse(QRectF(-35, -109, 70, 14))
        painter.setPen(Qt.PenStyle.NoPen)
        for (x, y), state in zip(PARTICLES, self.particle_states(bed, seconds)):
            depth = max(0, 1 - (x / 33) ** 2) ** .5
            colour = QColor(ACID if state else self.COPPER)
            colour.setAlpha(round(100 + 155 * depth))
            painter.setBrush(colour)
            radius = 1.45 + 1.4 * depth
            painter.drawEllipse(QPointF(x, y), radius, radius)

        painter.setBrush(Qt.BrushStyle.NoBrush)
        for _, front, colour in helices:
            colour.setAlpha(175)
            painter.setPen(QPen(colour, .85))
            painter.drawPath(front)
        painter.setPen(QPen(QColor("#8c9677"), .65))
        for end in (-108, 108):
            painter.drawEllipse(QRectF(-44, end - 7, 88, 14))
        painter.restore()

    def paintEvent(self, event):
        painter = QPainter(self)
        painter.setRenderHint(QPainter.RenderHint.Antialiasing)
        painter.fillRect(self.rect(), QColor(INK))
        width, height = self.width(), self.height()
        painter.save()
        scale = min((width - 44) / 520, (height - 112) / 270)
        painter.translate(width / 2, height / 2 - 4)
        painter.scale(scale, scale)
        painter.rotate(-12)

        # A quiet recurring contour ties the triptych together without arrows.
        painter.setBrush(Qt.BrushStyle.NoBrush)
        painter.setPen(QPen(QColor("#61694c"), 1))
        painter.drawEllipse(QRectF(-252, -72, 504, 144))
        seconds = self.seconds
        for bed in range(3):
            self._bed(painter, bed, seconds)
        painter.restore()

        font = QFont(font_family("Cascadia Mono", "Consolas", "DejaVu Sans Mono"))
        font.setPixelSize(11)
        painter.setFont(font)
        painter.setPen(QColor("#b7c0a2"))
        painter.drawText(22, 28, "REACTION / REGENERATION")
        painter.drawText(22, height - 24, "CYCLING STATES")
        painter.setPen(QPen(QColor(ACID), 1))
        painter.drawLine(width - 29, 23, width - 19, 23)
        painter.drawLine(width - 24, 18, width - 24, 28)
